column14: THE TITLE NAMES A PHENOTYPE THE MODEL DOES NOT REPRESENT AND THE LITERATURE DOES NOT ESTABLISH FOR THESE SPECIES. The new title is accurate on both halves: RADIORESISTANCE is what the published D10 evidence supports and what the per-species parameter magnitudes are anchored to; RADIOTROPIC FITNESS is what compute_delta_H implements, a directional preference along a dose gradient. Radiotrophy is neither evidenced (NEWS-AUD-05) nor representable (NEWS-PHEN-02). The file preprint/modeling_radiotrophic_fitness.{md,tex} still carries the old name.

column3: docs/calibration/integration_contract.md 'Which radiation phenotype this model actually represents'
column4: the CPM radiation term represents RADIOTROPISM - directional redistribution along a dose gradient
column14: THE CORRECTED READING OF A TERM THAT WAS ALREADY IN THE CODE. compute_delta_H adds beta_ion[s]*I_gamma when a parcel GAINS a site, so a negative beta lowers the Hamiltonian in high-dose sites and the parcel drifts UP the gradient; a positive beta drifts it down. That is a TROPISM and nothing else. The former in-source justification 'we use negative effective beta to represent metabolic energy gain' conflated a Metropolis acceptance functional in ARBITRARY UNITS with an energy budget, and has been removed (commit 01b0f4d). Kept, not restated: the statement as it now stands in the contract is correct and requires no further action.

column4: radiotrophic (radiation measurably ENHANCES growth or metabolism) is NOT represented
column14: STRUCTURALLY ABSENT, NOT WEAKLY SUPPORTED. There is no growth in the model: divide_cell! is called from nowhere, no biomass is created, and no fitness variable is computed anywhere. A model with no birth cannot express a growth enhancement, and NO QUANTITY OF DATA CHANGES THAT WITHOUT A MODEL REVISION. This is unsupported_by_current_model, the same class as response.growth_survival - not blocked. blocked awaits a measurement; unsupported awaits a model change.

column4: radioresistant (elevated SURVIVAL after exposure) is NOT represented
column14: STRUCTURALLY ABSENT for the mirror-image reason to NEWS-PHEN-02: there is no death. The only death path is volume <= 0 while lambda_V = 10 drives every parcel toward V_target = 120, so no parcel dies and survival has no representation. This is the sharpest instance of the discipline in the whole repository: the evidence for radioresistance is EXCELLENT (D10 for D. radiodurans ~12 kGy, for S. oneidensis ~0.07 kGy, both well sourced) and the model still cannot express it. Good data plus no representation is unsupported_by_current_model, not a calibration opportunity.

column4: the published D10 radioresistance evidence anchors the per-species beta_ion magnitudes
column13: Declare the substitution wherever beta_ion is tabulated, and give the tropism weight its own symbol
column14: RADIORESISTANCE EVIDENCE SPENT ON A TROPISM COEFFICIENT. The D10 literature is strong and it is the only quantitative anchor the beta_ion column has - but a survival coefficient in 1/Gy and a signed dimensionless spatial preference in a Metropolis test are different quantities, and one cannot calibrate the other. The substitution is LEGITIMATE ONLY AS A DECLARED MODELLING CHOICE, and it is now declared in the contract rather than left implicit in a sign convention. This is why the retitle keeps both words: the evidence is radioresistance, the mechanism is radiotropism.

column4: the model's tropism is MELANIN-MEDIATED: radiation -> production (alpha_M, tabulated) -> M -> dH_mel (0.5, untabulated) -> tropism
column14: THE CORRECTED HEADLINE FINDING, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES. An earlier draft concluded that radiation does not reach the dynamics. IT DOES - through melanin: melanin_drive is copied from the radiation field, so the radiation field sets melanin production, and melanin production drives the acceptance term that dominates by four orders of magnitude. What is false is the tabulated pathway, not the phenomenon. Two consequences worth stating in the paper: a sensitivity analysis over beta_ion would report the radiation response as negligible and be RIGHT ABOUT THE COEFFICIENT WHILE WRONG ABOUT THE MECHANISM; and a parameter that decides the headline result must not live only at its call site.

column14: STRUCTURAL, NOT A DATA PROBLEM. Only the PRODUCT alpha_M * k reaches the dynamics, so no experiment that observes only the trajectory can separate the two factors. Any future fit must either fix one by independent measurement (pigmentation versus exposure, which is what response.melanin would supply) or report the product and say so. Recording this now prevents a later fit from reporting a precise value for either factor alone.

column14: Verdict of a seven-track retrieval audit, each track independently re-verified; the verification pass governs and disagreements are recorded rather than resolved. Radiotrophy is claimed for two of the seven species and the claim rests on ONE 2007 paper whose exposure was a 188Re beta field characterised BY ANALOGY rather than by a stated dosimeter, whose growth effects are single-digit percentages, and whose integrated cell dose is not stated. Against it: a same-species report of no substantial melanin protection under gamma, a same-species negative melanin-pathway result at 1 and 3 kGy, a same-genus null under a TLD-anchored 137Cs field, an isogenic null in A. niger across three modalities, and a formal energy-budget critique. No public dataset closes this; only a targeted experiment does.

The seed depended only on (draw, replicate), never on the material state, so with feedback_elements = None the two models were bit-identical and the metric returned ~1e-16 at any energy, for any physics, however broken the transport. column4: The unsigned relative-L2 metric has a noise floor of 0.0545 at the finest mesh and 1e5 histories per run, scaling as 1/sqrt(N).

Three history budgets (1e5, 4e5, 1.6e6 per run) give f=1 floors 0.05449, 0.02785, 0.01324 - successive ratios 1.96 and 2.10 against the 2.0 expected from 1/sqrt(N), holding at every mesh factor. The metric is unsigned, so this is a positive BIAS that never cancels, distinct from the replicate SCATTER the budget's transport term reports (sd 0.0023, 24x smaller). Four of the six tabulated material levers sit below this floor.

The numerator was np.var(by_factor, ddof=1) over exactly TWO mesh factors, which is algebraically (d1-d0)^2/2 - a squared difference, not a variance. It reproduces (0.15125673-0.12362119)^2/2 = 3.8186e-04 to every digit. The denominator was a genuine multi-replicate variance. column4: The per-factor spread survived the occupancy fix, which is how we know the 22% is genuine discretisation rather than a masking artifact.
column13: Equalise the uncertainty criterion too, then restate
column14: HALF RIGHT, AND THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES THE OTHER HALF. The occupancy criterion had been equalised; the UNCERTAINTY criterion had not. omega_b also required rel_err < 0.25, which bit the factors unequally - at f=1 it removed about a third of the bins (983/949/968 of 8000, median rel_err 0.1837) while at f=2 it never bound (a constant 215/1000, median 0.0837). Membership therefore also moved with the history count, so the metric's domain changed with its precision. rel_err is now a diagnostic, not a membership criterion; f=1 bin counts rose from ~965 to ~1500, and the f=1 to f=2 movement is still 22% (0.1237 to 0.1509). The claim was right; the evidence offered for it did not support it.

column4: With numerics at 97.7% of the variance, quadrupling the histories buys a 0.7% component; the budget belongs in mesh resolution.
column13: Recommend the 4e6 history setting - the noise floor, not the replicate scatter, is what histories buy down
column14: THE RECOMMENDATION IS REVERSED. The 97.7% compared a discretisation BOUND against a replicate SCATTER and omitted the noise BIAS entirely. The bias is 0.0545 at the pilot's settings, it scales as 1/sqrt(N) (verified over a 16x history range), and it is the quantity deciding whether an effect of 0.02-0.05 - where every physically realistic lever sits - is measurable at all. About 40x the pilot's histories are needed to push the floor below 0.01. Discretisation still dominates scatter by ~25x in effect units, so the A0 lesson holds; the inference drawn from it did not.

column4: The gate decides on a cross-replicate debiased squared effect, not on the raw unsigned relative-L2 norm.
column14: UNBIASED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY SUBTRACTION. Across independent replicates E[d_r^T W d_s] = E[d_r]^T W E[d_s], so the estimator carries no noise term to estimate and remove. The denominator uses the same cross-replicate construction because E[||D0_r||^2_W] carries the baseline's own noise power and a naive squared norm is biased HIGH. Reported squared and compared against delta^2: taking a root near zero reintroduces the bias. S_hat MAY BE NEGATIVE and must be, about half the time, when the true effect is zero - the noise_floor scenario returned 8 negative of 16 draws - exactly half. Verified against simulation at the measured geometry: at a true effect of 0.020 the raw norm reads 0.0223-0.0294 while the debiased estimate recovers 0.0200 at every R from 3 to 20.

column4: Under the debiased estimator the noise-floor scenario is not distinguishable from zero.
column14: THE CONTROL NOW BEHAVES LIKE A CONTROL. The same scenario reads 0.0653 under the raw unsigned norm and is indistinguishable from zero under the debiased statistic, on the same runs and the same seeds - which is the cleanest available demonstration that the 0.0653 was the metric's bias and not a physical effect. Significance now comes from the estimator's own jackknife standard error rather than from a comparison against another scenario, so the retired 3x-floor rule cannot acquire the status of an undeclared second threshold.

Against the raw f=1 values in PILOT-LEV-02: density x1.35 drops 0.02443 -> 0.00743 (-70%) and 5% Fe 0.00488 -> 0.00253 (-48%), while the two strong levers barely move (5% Gd -3.5%, dehydration -2%). Paired and unpaired estimates now AGREE where the unpaired one has the precision to say so (Gd 5%: 0.03652 vs 0.03344), whereas under the raw norm they differed by 13-83%; common random numbers now buy precision only, tightening the standard error by 8x to 140x without moving the estimate.

column13: State that this sized the RAW norm's bias, and that the debiased estimator is unbiased at the current history count
column14: MY OWN CORRECTION, CORRECTED. PILOT-COST-01 reversed the original recommendation from 'histories buy nothing' to 'buy ~40x more', on the ground that the noise BIAS is what decides whether a 0.02-0.05 effect is measurable. That reasoning was right about the raw norm and is superseded for the gate: the debiased estimator is unbiased at R = 3 and at the pilot's existing history count, so histories now buy PRECISION rather than correctness. Simulation and the run agree - 5% Gd is resolved at z = 46 and dehydration at z = 26 with 1e5 histories per run. More histories remain worth buying to tighten the standard error and to reduce the discretisation bound, which still dominates the budget (numerics 9.2e-04 against transport 7.7e-07 in E^2), but they are no longer a precondition for measuring the small levers at all.

column4: A declared effect threshold is interpretable without naming the metric it is denominated in.
column13: metric_id on the policy and an optional metric_id argument to decide()
column14: A THRESHOLD IS NOT TRANSFERABLE BETWEEN METRICS AND NOTHING ABOUT THE NUMBER REVEALS IT. Moving the gate from a relative L2 effect to a debiased SQUARED effect changes 0.10 into 0.01 and 0.02 into 0.0004; comparing an E-denominated threshold against E^2 draws is a silent factor-of-ten error that no test on the numbers alone would catch. ThresholdPolicy now carries metric_id, problems() refuses an empty one, and decide() returns NOT_EVALUATED when the draws' metric_id does not match the policy's.

column4: The committed effect table records which run produced it.
column13: A provenance header on every committed table - done
column14: IT RECORDED NOTHING. The header carried prose semantics only: no commit, no OpenMC version, no nuclear-data identity, no history count, no timestamp. The sibling JSONs that did carry provenance live under artifacts/, which is gitignored, so they were never committed and the table was provenance-orphaned. Both committed CSVs now carry a provenance block. Note the structural limit stated there: an artifact CANNOT name the commit that will contain it, so git_commit names the PARENT and carries the -dirty marker; that pair plus the config and snapshot hashes is the honest identity.

column4: The cross_sections.xml checksum is recorded in ~/openmc-data/*.sha256.
column13: Record the archive checksum, which is what exists and is the stronger identity
column14: ONLY THE ARCHIVE CHECKSUM EXISTS (endfb-viii.0-hdf5.tar.xz.sha256); there is no checksum for cross_sections.xml. The archive digest is the better identity anyway since it pins every data file rather than only the index. Related: synthetic_e2e.py writes the LITERAL string 'endfb-viii.0' rather than reading OPENMC_CROSS_SECTIONS, so it records an assumption about the environment rather than an observation of it. openmc_nested_pilot.py:_nuclear_data_id() resolves the env var and its recorded digest and names the file the digest came from.

column4: Factor 1 is the finest tally available; the mesh cannot be refined below the CPM lattice pitch.
column13: A refinement path in resolve_mesh_dimension - done
column14: IT WAS ARITHMETIC, NOT PHYSICS, AND THE REPORT STATED IT AS A PROPERTY OF THE MODEL. An openmc.RegularMesh sets its physical extent and its bin count independently; biofilm_mesh_extent_cm() already ignored the dimension and mesh_material_volumes raytraces whatever mesh it is given. What blocked refinement was `return tuple(d // f for d in base)` with no multiplicative path. Tally ratios 1x, 2x and 4x now build, raytrace and run. A finer tally adds TRANSPORT resolution only - the material lattice stays piecewise constant at the CPM pitch - so this answers the discretisation question and says nothing about morphology.

column4: The mass-weighted relative-L2 effect metric is not resolution-invariant and does not converge under tally refinement.
column6: E = 0.12280 at 1x, 0.12305 at 2x, 0.10555 at 4x (identical region, 5 replicates, 3.2e5 particles)
column14: MEASURED OVER AN IDENTICAL REGION AND CONFIRMED HISTORY-INDEPENDENT. Omega_b is defined once at the lattice resolution and upsampled, so the three ratios cover exactly the same physical volume (1562 / 12496 / 99968 bins, exactly x8 and x64). The 4x result is stable to 0.3% across a 16x history range while the per-bin relative error falls 0.736 -> 0.222, so it is not a noise artifact. Decomposing the ratio explains it: refining 1x -> 4x grows the numerator ||E[d]||^2_W by 1.55 and the DENOMINATOR ||E[D0]||^2_W by 2.10, because the baseline field carries the steep gradients of an axial line source and every material boundary while the difference field is smoother. CONSEQUENCE: a declared effect threshold is only meaningful alongside a declared tally resolution, exactly as it is only meaningful alongside a metric_id. Quoting 0.12 without one quotes a number that moves 48% across the resolutions measured (0.1055 at 4x to 0.1821 at coarsening factor 5).

column4: 72% of the baseline dose field's mass-weighted L2 norm lies below the CPM lattice pitch.
column14: DEBIASED, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT IS BELIEVABLE. Measured as the cross-replicate inner product of the residual about each voxel's own mass-weighted mean, so Monte Carlo noise contributes nothing in expectation. The naive single-replicate version reads 1.05 at 4x and is almost pure noise, since the per-bin relative error there is 0.74. Stable to 0.15% across a 16x history range. This is a statement about TRANSPORT structure within a parcel of uniform material, not about morphology - the CPM asserts uniform material inside a voxel, so dose structure below that scale is arguably a detail the biology cannot see, which is why the report recommends declaring the tally at the lattice pitch and carrying the 4x value as a BOUND.

column4: Heating scored in a bin with zero mass always means the tally and the geometry disagree.
column13: Refuse by magnitude rather than by presence
column14: A ZERO RAYTRACED VOLUME IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A PROOF OF EMPTINESS. The guard treated an O(1/sqrt(n)) raytrace estimate as ground truth and so refused correct runs: at 4x refinement, 1-2 bins in 512 000 receive heating in a material sliver too thin for any ray to strike, carrying at most 6.5e-07 of the total. Buying rays does not fix it - 5.12e6 rays leaves the massless-bin count at 25.25% against 25.38% at 1.6e6, because most massless bins are the genuinely void corners of a cube circumscribing a cylinder (1 - pi/4 = 21.5%). The guard now refuses above a 1e-4 share and warns below it, discarding the orphaned energy rather than redistributing it. A real disagreement - misaligned mesh, wrong extent, transposed axis - puts percent-level or more there and still raises, three orders of magnitude above the tolerance.

column4: Raytrace accuracy improves monotonically with n_samples, so scale it with the bin count.
column13: Choose verified counts: n_samples = P * dim^2, not P * dim^3
column14: TWO SEPARATE ERRORS IN THAT ASSUMPTION. (1) Each ray crosses `dim` bins along its axis, so n_samples = P*dim^2 already delivers about P samples per bin - per-bin sampling does not fall as dim^3 and scaling that way overshoots by the linear dimension. (2) Raising the count is not safe: material_volumes lays rays on a regular grid, and at some counts a ray passes within floating-point epsilon of a lattice plane and OpenMC ABORTS THE PROCESS with 'could not be located after crossing a boundary of lattice'. That abort is not a catchable exception. It is neither monotone in ray count nor related to refinement - 20^3 bins abort at 2.56e6 rays while 80^3 bins succeed at 5.12e6 - and setting max_lost_particles does not help because material_volumes runs through openmc.lib.init and never reads it. The counts in use are individually verified.

column4: Block-summing a refined tally back to the lattice grid reproduces the unrefined result exactly.
column14: THE CHECK PASSED FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN THE ONE GIVEN. It compared only the E^2 statistic, and E^2 is a ratio in which the mass denominator appears in both sums and cancels to high order - so it agreed to nine significant figures while the underlying DOSE FIELD differed by 1.5%, because each ratio raytraced its own mass denominator and independent raytraces of the same geometry differ by up to 3.0% per voxel. Every ratio now shares ONE raytrace, taken at the finest ratio and coarsened down (mass is extensive, so that is exact and also cheaper). With that, the field-level identity holds: mass 4.8e-16, heating 6.0e-16, dose field 5.6e-16. The driver now asserts on the FIELD at 1e-9. The headline E^2 values are unchanged to six digits by the fix, which is itself the evidence that E^2 was insensitive to the denominator.

column4: Raytracing the CSG volumes independently at each tally resolution gives each resolution a correct mass denominator.
column13: One raytrace at the finest ratio, coarsened down - done
column14: CORRECT PER RATIO, INCONSISTENT ACROSS THEM, AND DOSE IS HEATING OVER MASS. Independent raytraces of the same geometry differ by up to 3.0% per voxel and 0.13% in total, so every ratio's dose field inherited a different denominator and the ratios differed for a reason unrelated to resolution. Mass is extensive, so coarsening the finest estimate is exact; it also costs one raytrace instead of one per ratio. Measured consequence: with the shared raytrace the reduced 4x dose field matches the native 1x field to 5.6e-16, against 1.5e-02 before.

column4: A multi-grid viewer bundle in which upsampled layers may be drawn and may not be quoted.
column14: THE DIRECTION OF RESAMPLING IS WHAT DECIDES QUOTABILITY, and an earlier draft of this rule was blunter than the physics. UPSAMPLING broadcasts one value across bins that were never separately measured - it INVENTS information, and is refused authoritative_for_quantitation whatever the arithmetic. REDUCTION (block sum of an extensive quantity, mass-weighted mean of an intensive one) destroys information and invents none: the refinement study confirms a 4x dose field reduced to the lattice reproduces the native lattice field to 5.6e-16, so forbidding it would be wrong. A 'reduction' onto a grid that is not coarser is refused, since that label is the only thing standing between upsampling and being quoted. Also enforced: one origin and one physical extent across all grids in a bundle, integer dtype for categorical layers, no arithmetic resampling of labels, and no blank units.

column4: The repository can produce a viewer bundle containing a genuinely native high-resolution dose field.
column14: BEFORE THE REFINEMENT WORK THERE WAS NOTHING TO SHOW. The only producer was synthetic_e2e.py, which upsamples a coarse dose field to lattice resolution BEFORE attribution, so a viewer could have displayed only the lattice grid and anything finer would have been a coarse field broadcast to look detailed. The bundle now carries cpm_labels (20^3) alongside native OpenMC dose grids at 20^3, 40^3 and 80^3, all spanning the identical 24.0 cm cube with one origin, plus both sides of the resampling rule on real data: a mass-weighted reduction marked quotable and an upsampled label overlay marked not. Written from the refinement run's own in-memory fields, so it costs no extra transport.

column4: Discarding heating from massless bins costs nothing measurable.
column13: State that the discard is resolution-dependent and record the drift per row
column14: IT COSTS LITTLE, AND IT IS RESOLUTION-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KNOWING. The sliver tolerance in dose.specific_energy_per_source drops heating found in bins the raytrace gave zero volume. That drop depends on the tally resolution: at 4x a sliver is its own bin and its energy is discarded, while at 1x the same energy sits inside a coarse voxel with mass and is kept - so the reduced 4x field and the native 1x field differ. FIRST EXPLANATION REACHED FOR WAS FLOAT ACCUMULATION, AND IT WAS WRONG: accumulation would put the 8-term and 64-term sums ~8x apart, not four orders of magnitude. Localisation confirms the real mechanism - of the voxels carrying drift above 1% of the maximum there is EXACTLY ONE, holding 28 of its 64 sub-bins massless, against 19% of the remaining voxels holding any; mass itself conserves to 4.8e-16. Magnitude is negligible for this study (3.0e-09 against a 27% finding) but it is now recorded per row as lattice_field_drift_vs_ratio1 rather than assumed.

column4: The S0 verdict may be computed from effect draws pooled across tally resolutions.
column6: 16 rows = 4 outer draws x 4 mesh factors
column13: Gate on the finest resolution, widened by the residual discretisation bound - done
column14: THIS IS THE ONE THAT REACHED THE VERDICT. Pooling put a systematic, monotone discretisation trend inside a distribution the gate reads as sampling spread, and mesh_coarsening_factor is declared sampling_role = convergence_axis precisely so it is never drawn from. The trend is large: clearly_detectable runs 5.05e-2 at f=1 to 8.09e-2 at f=5, a 60% drift and ~71x the correct standard error; lever_density_x1.35 spans 6e-5 to 7.5e-4, 13.5x. CRITICALLY, gating on the finest factor ALONE is a RELAXATION, not a fix: lever_density_x1.35's 99% upper bound falls 7.59e-4 -> 7.12e-5, under the 4e-4 practical floor, converting 'real but not worth acting on' into 'below threshold' by looking at less. decide() therefore takes a resolution_bound and widens the interval symmetrically. Under finest+bound no verdict in the committed run becomes easier and three become stricter.

column4: distinguishable_from_zero used e2 > 3 * sqrt(mean(jackknife_var)) as a significance test.
column13: Cluster-on-outer-draw SE at the finest mesh, with a t critical value - done
column14: THREE ERRORS IN ONE LINE, AND THE DIRECTION WAS OPPOSITE TO THE ONE FIRST ASSUMED. (1) It pooled over outer draws AND mesh factors. (2) sqrt(mean(jackknife_var)) is the rms standard error of ONE row - no 1/sqrt(M), no between-draw term - so it is not the standard error of the mean it divided into. (3) '3 sigma' on M-1 = 3 degrees of freedom is a ~94% one-sided test wearing a 99.9% label; the t critical value is 10.21. Measured against a cluster SE on the committed run, the old se is CONSERVATIVE in 10 of 11 scenarios (2.06x to 10.15x) and anti-conservative in exactly one (lever_dehydration_H_0.06, 0.87x), so it produced NO false positives here - the initial analysis claimed anti-conservatism of 2-20x and was refuted by data already in the repo. The per-row jackknife spread is kept under its own name because it is the right input to VarianceBudget.transport, and it is labelled a floor rather than an estimate: the delete-one jackknife on a RATIO overstates the true per-row SD by ~1.8x at R = 3.

column4: Omega_b required a dose floor taken from replicate 0's field.
column13: Two geometric criteria only - done
column14: THE SAME ERROR THE MODULE HAD ALREADY LEARNED ONCE, IN A SUBTLER FORM. The first version cut on rel_err and the docstring was rewritten to say MEMBERSHIP MUST NOT DEPEND ON THE ESTIMATOR; the dose floor then violated that rule while the docstring asserted it. Because the floor came from one replicate, the region was a random set drawn from that replicate, so 2(R-1) of the R(R-1) ordered pairs the U-statistic averages involve a row that helped choose the weights - four of six at R = 3. Magnitude is P3 (well under 1% of E^2, inside one standard error) and no verdict moves on this alone, but the floor was also doing almost no work: sub-floor biomass bins carry a fraction of a percent of the weighted norm. Dropping it shifts the estimand by up to 11% in one scenario, so it rides the same regeneration. NOTE: a floor computed from the replicate MEAN is not a fix - it correlates membership with every row instead of one.

column4: The debiased squared effect is an unbiased estimate of the squared relative effect.
column13: Scope the claim to the numerator and denominator; record the bias SCALE, not a point estimate
column14: THE NUMERATOR AND DENOMINATOR ARE EACH UNBIASED; THEIR RATIO IS NOT. E[X/Y] != E[X]/E[Y], and the two are correlated through the baseline rows they share, giving the usual delta-method term Var(Den)/E[Den]^2 - Cov(S,Den)/(E[S]E[Den]) at O(1/R). What is recorded is the SCALE, |bias|/SD ~ relerr*sqrt(2(1-rho)/(R*B_eff)) < 3e-2 across the envelope (R 3-5, relerr 0.03-0.74, rho 0-0.9), rather than a point estimate that depends on an assumed rho. B_eff is the PARTICIPATION RATIO (sum w mu^2)^2/(sum w^2 mu^4) ~ 400, not the bin count ~1500: a dose field concentrated near a line source has far fewer effective bins than bins, and using the bin count understates the bias ~2x. NO PLUG-IN CORRECTION IS SHIPPED - both the delta-method and jackknife corrections were measured and both are harmful at small R, turning -35% into +170% in the stress regime. rho measured here at 0.93-1.00 from the paired/unpaired lever pairs, against 0.855-0.932 measured from replicate residuals; the bound is small either way.

column4: A PyVista observer that renders a viewer bundle and computes nothing.
column6: 14 of 16 tests in the bare tier
column14: ALMOST NONE OF A VIEWER IS RENDERING, WHICH IS WHY ALMOST ALL OF IT IS TESTABLE WITHOUT ONE. Choosing which layers may be drawn, what each must be labelled with, how a categorical field maps to colour, where a grid sits in centimetres and what the provenance panel says are decisions about DATA. PyVista is imported function-locally in exactly two entry points, so 14 of 16 tests run with no renderer installed; only to_image_data and plot_layer are gated. The module imports neither feedback_uq nor synthetic_gate and a test asserts it ON THE IMPORT GRAPH rather than the text, since the docstring names the modules it refuses. A non-quotable layer carries a REQUIRED banner naming the mechanism, and plot_layer RAISES rather than warns if a caller suppresses it. Arrays attach as CELL data, never point data: interpolating a piecewise-constant voxel field to points would smooth the material boundaries the model asserts are sharp and make a categorical field meaningless. Species palette and orbit camera carried across from the feat/visualize-3d prototype, which is otherwise unusable.

column4: A layer is quotable only if it is both native and authoritative_for_quantitation.
column13: Key on authoritative_for_quantitation alone
column14: A LEFTOVER FROM THE BLUNTER FIRST RULE, AND IT DEMOTED EXACTLY THE CASE THE SHARPENED RULE PERMITS. When the contract was corrected to allow a reduction to stay quotable - an exact mass-weighted reduction reproduces the native field at that resolution to 5.6e-16 - bundle_problems was updated and quantitative_layers was not, so a derived-but-authoritative layer was silently excluded. `native` is descriptive; `authoritative_for_quantitation` is the field named for the decision, and bundle_problems already guarantees it cannot be set on an upsampling. CAUGHT BY RUNNING THE OBSERVER AGAINST THE REAL BUNDLE, where dose_on_lattice_from_r4 was labelled NOT QUANTITATIVE; the existing test passed either way because its fixture used a non-authoritative layer. Quotable count on the committed bundle moves 13 -> 15 of 17.

column4: specific_interface_area_per_um measures a physical interface area density.
column13: Redenominate the tolerance against a same-pitch reference, or replace the estimator
column14: IT MEASURES THE INTEGRAL OF |n|_1 OVER THE SURFACE, NOT |n|_2, SO IT IS NOT AN AREA AND NO REFINEMENT FIXES IT. Counting axis-aligned faces gives a ratio to the true area equal to E[|n|_1] for the surface's orientation distribution. Verified on three geometries at three pitches each: axis-aligned plane 1.0000/1.0000/1.0000 against a predicted 1; 45-degree plane 1.4001/1.4071/1.4107 against sqrt(2)=1.4142; isotropic sphere 1.5096/1.5011/1.5006 against 3*E|n_x|=3/2. Three orientations, three different constants, each matched within 2% and converging TOWARD the constant rather than toward 1. On the sphere ladder the relative error against a closed-form area sits at 0.467-0.510 across an 8x pitch range and is slightly WORSE at the finest pitch. (RESTATED per LADDER-06: the original 0.41-0.51 over 16x took both of its bounds from the 3.2 um row that LADDER-04 withdrew for not tiling the spheres' 24 um axis. The narrower spread over a shorter range does not weaken the finding - the error moves LESS than was reported while still refusing to fall.) CONSEQUENCE: maximum_interface_area_error = 0.10 is declared `hard` in config/reference_d_spatial_acceptance.toml and NO pitch can satisfy it against a physical area for any curved interface. The tolerance is denominated in the wrong thing rather than set wrongly - select_pitch compares the SAME estimator on a reference and a coarsened copy, where the ~1.5 factor largely cancels. NOTE the cancellation is only PARTIAL, because coarsening changes the orientation statistics of the discretised surface.

column4: Specific interface area falls 46% at coarsening factor 2 on the V. cholerae pilot.
column14: SURVIVES LADDER-01, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING. That result compares ONE estimator at TWO pitches, not an estimator against a physical area, so the ~1.5 orientation factor is present in both terms and largely cancels. It therefore measures real resolution loss, which is what it was quoted for. It would NOT survive being read as 'the interface area fell 46% in physical units', and nothing in the pilot claims that.

column4: The coarsest pitch preserving each declared observable, measured against closed-form truth.
column6: component size 3.2 um, biovolume 0.8 um, porosity 0.4 um, interface area never
column14: THE FIRST MEASUREMENT OF WHAT A PITCH COSTS AGAINST A KNOWN ANSWER. select_pitch has never had this, because on real data there is no truth to compare against. Nine spheres of radius 5 um on a 16 um lattice in a 48x48x24 um box, five pitches from 3.2 to 0.2 um, occupancy thresholded at the frozen tau = 0.5. Porosity needing a 2x finer pitch than biovolume is the `derived` tolerance working as intended: porosity is 1 - biovolume, so an equal relative tolerance is ~20x tighter and the config carries a separately derived 0.0025. An axis-aligned slab is EXACT at every pitch (errors 0 to 2e-16), which is the control establishing that the sphere errors are about curvature and not about the ladder machinery. CALIBRATES THE METHOD, NEVER THE SPECIMEN: the objects are invented, so this says what a pitch costs a measurement, not what pitch a biofilm needs. SUPERSEDED IN PART BY LADDER-04: the 3.2 um pitch in this row's ladder does not tile the spheres' 24 um axis and was withdrawn; the coarsest pitch preserving component size is 1.6 um and not 3.2. The biovolume (0.8) and porosity (0.4) figures are unaffected, having been measured at pitches that tile.

column4: The gate refuses a growth condition without an institutional biosafety approval.
column13: Check what a reviewer would ask for, not that a string is non-empty
column14: IT WAS A PRESENCE CHECK, AND SINCE THE SCHEMA ALREADY REFUSED A BLANK IT WAS VERY NEARLY A NO-OP. institutional_approval_id is required=True in BASELINE_CONDITION, so read_table already rejected an empty cell; what the gate added was nothing, because ANY non-empty string passed. It accepted 'approved', 'pending', 'TBD', and the literal words 'd approved' -- which is how the hole was found, when that phrase was offered as an approval and refused by a human rather than by the code. It would equally have accepted a real-looking identifier belonging to another protocol, covering different strains, at another facility, issued after culturing, or expired. Replaced by calibration/biofilm_calibration/approval.py.

column4: The approval checks verify that an institutional biosafety approval is genuine.
column13: State what the checks do and do not establish
column14: THEY DO NOT AND CANNOT VERIFY AUTHENTICITY. What they verify is that the fields a reviewer would ask for are present, resolve, agree with one another, and still describe the row: filler text refused by value; an issuing authority named; approval_source_id resolving to a document_type = institutional_biosafety_approval row with a url or digest; ISO dates satisfying effective <= culturing_start < expiration with today < expiration; and approval_scope_hash matching a digest over the approved scope columns. No check local to this repository can establish that a committee issued a document. THE SCOPE DIGEST DETECTS DRIFT, NOT FORGERY: anyone who edits a growth condition AND recomputes the hash defeats it. What it makes impossible is editing a condition and silently inheriting an approval that never covered it, which is the failure that happens by accident.

column4: Reference D readiness is a function of the repository state alone.
column13: Print the evaluation date; inject it in tests
column14: AN APPROVAL EXPIRES, SO THE VERDICT NOW DEPENDS ON WHEN IT IS ASKED. A run that passes this week can fail next week with no code or data change, and that is correct -- a lapsed approval authorises nothing. Two consequences are handled explicitly rather than discovered later: the status report PRINTS the date it judged against, so a changed verdict is explainable instead of alarming; and `today` is an injected parameter throughout approval.problems and spatial report.evaluate, so tests pin a fixed date and do not become time bombs.

column4: A source_id resolving successfully establishes that the cited document is the right document.
column13: document_type with a controlled vocabulary, plus sha256
column14: IT ESTABLISHED ONLY THAT SOMETHING WITH THAT ID WAS REGISTERED. An approval field could cite NIST_WATER -- a real id, resolving cleanly, and a cross-section table -- and pass. That is the 'belongs to another protocol' failure with nothing in the data able to see it. The registry now carries document_type against a shared vocabulary in physical_contract (APPROVAL_DOCUMENT_TYPES) and sha256, and the approval check requires the resolved row to be an approval kind with a url or digest. The three existing rows are declarations and were backfilled as such; none is a retrieved file, so their digests are genuinely absent rather than unknown. NOTE the target is the SPATIAL BRANCH registry, not data/sources.csv, which no calibration code reads by design.

column4: The claims-ledger guard checks 30 of the 34 `delete` claims.
column13: Report DETECTION against a document known to contain the claims, not phrase count
column14: IT COUNTED ROWS THAT YIELD A SEARCHABLE PHRASE, NOT ROWS THE GUARD CAN FIND. Real coverage is 20 of 34. An external review (Codex, PR #11) raised the mechanism as P1: the ledger records claims as prose ('using DifferentialEquations.jl') while the sources carry markup ('using \\texttt{DifferentialEquations.jl}' in LaTeX, backticked in the Markdown derivative), so a raw substring search misses a claim restored the way anyone would write it. Measured against the pre-revision originals, normalising markup lifts detection from 12 to 15 of 30 in the .tex and 15 to 20 of 30 in the .md. MY FIRST ATTEMPT TO MEASURE THE DAMAGE WAS ALSO WRONG and nearly produced a second false conclusion: I ran the guard against HEAD~2 of the old .tex and got 1/30, which is the ALREADY-REVISED file, never a valid control. The conclusion that the current manuscript carries none of the deleted claims still stands, because it was verified separately against the RENDERED text via pdftotext, where markup does not survive. The guard was broken; the manual check was not.

column4: The guard is calibrated against a document known to contain the deleted claims.
column14: A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A CHECK, and the first version of this guard could not. test_no_deleted_claim_survives_in_the_manuscript passes when it finds nothing, which a broken guard also does. The control runs it against the manuscript as first committed (5980dc5), the one document known to contain the claims, and requires at least 18 detections: measured 20 with markup normalisation, against 15 without, so a regression to raw substring matching fails here rather than silently halving the guard. Verified directly - 20 survivors reported against the pre-revision manuscript, 0 against the current one.

column4: The coarsest pitch preserving component size is 3.2 um.
column13: Refuse a pitch that does not tile the declared extent; the answer is 1.6 um
column14: THE ROW WAS MEASURING A DIFFERENT BOX. 3.2 um does not tile the spheres' 24 um axis (7.5 voxels) and _grid_shape ROUNDED to 8, so the rasterised object was 48x48x25.6 um while the closed-form truth kept dividing by the declared 48x48x24. A 6.7% denominator shift was reported as rasterisation error, in the one study whose entire purpose is to hold the object fixed and move only the sampling. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #9). A non-tiling pitch is now refused rather than rounded and the ladder NAMES the pitch it skipped. Component size moves 3.2 -> 1.6 um. SEE LADDER-06: this row originally made a blanket claim about how far the correction reached, which was wrong - the interface-area RANGE was also computed from the withdrawn row and moves to 0.467-0.510 across 8x. No blanket claim of that kind belongs in this row: the scope of 'unchanged' is exactly what went unchecked, and rewording the reassurance is how it survived two corrections.

column4: plot_layer renders every bundle layer with its declared colour rule.
column13: The function raised NameError on its first rendering line; it rendered nothing
column14: CATEGORICAL and BOOLEAN are defined in viewer.py and were never imported into observer.py, so every call on a machine with a renderer raised NameError. Nothing caught it: pyvista is installed neither in CI nor in the dev environment, so all eight render tests SKIPPED and the suite reported green over a dead function. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Fixed by the import plus a bare-tier test that resolves every global the render path uses, which fails without the import and needs no renderer.

column4: A criterion is unmet exactly when the gate has something to say about it.
column13: Unmapped refusals now fail criterion 6 and are named, instead of counting as met
column14: authorization_criteria mapped approval.problems to the nine criteria by substring and treated a refusal matching no pattern as evidence for nothing - so it DEFAULTED TO MET. Adding the approved_protocol_version check to the gate therefore produced a refusal the milestone could not see: verified by running it, the gate refused while 0 of 9 criteria were unmet, i.e. the institutional biosafety milestone read AUTHORIZED over a live refusal. This is the inverse of REFD-04 and worse. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). A parametrized negative control now breaks each approval field in turn and requires every refusal to reach some criterion.

column4: The ladder names the pitch it skipped rather than dropping the row.
column13: 3.2 restored to the default; the slab evaluates it and the spheres refuse it by name
column14: THE CORRECTION FOR LADDER-04 WAS ITSELF WRONG. It removed 3.2 from the default --pitches, which is not the same as refusing it. Two losses: 3.2 tiles the SLAB and that axis-aligned control row vanished, and run_ladder only emits its skipped row for a pitch it is handed, so the promise that the ladder names what it skipped became unreachable in the same commit that made it. A pitch absent from the list is indistinguishable from a pitch nobody tried. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). The component_size 3.2 -> 1.6 um correction in LADDER-04 is unaffected and stands.

column4: Categorical layers are thresholded at 0.5 to drop the background.
column13: The producer declares Layer.background; None means no cell may be hidden
column14: A blanket threshold at 0.5 deleted every zero-valued categorical cell. cell_id 0 is genuinely empty space, but the generation layer carries the note 'generation 0 is a founder, not a missing value' - the producer wrote the warning and the renderer ignored it, erasing the founding cohort from every picture of it. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Background is now declared by the code that built the field; a layer that declares none is drawn in full.

column4: A layer that declares no background is drawn in full.
column13: An ambiguous categorical layer names the layer that carries occupancy
column14: THE FIX FOR VIEW-03 OVERSHOT. export_checkpoint.jl zero-fills the generation array and skips unoccupied voxels, so generation 0 is BOTH a founder and empty space and no background VALUE can separate them: 0 deletes the founding cohort, None draws the void as generation-0 biomass. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12) on the fix for VIEW-03. Layer.occupancy_from now names the field that says where biomass is, and plot_layer masks by it using the pre-existing observer.occupied_mask, which tests > 0 rather than != 0 because -1 marks the wall.

column4: The gate refuses a merge while any review thread is unresolved.
column13: Every severity blocks, including P3 and unranked
column14: The first version listed P1|P2|UNRANKED as the failing cases, so a pull request whose only open thread was P3 printed 'Clear to merge' while contradicting the script's own documented contract. A check that could not fail, inside the check written to stop checks that cannot fail. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Severity ranks what to fix first, not what may be ignored. The gate now ships with negative controls run in CI, including a synthetic unresolved P3, plus two positive controls so a gate that refused everything could not pass them.

column4: occupancy_from names the layer that carries occupancy.
column13: A dangling, cross-grid or doubly-declared reference is refused at write time
column14: Nothing validated occupancy_from, though the adjacent source_grid_id check has existed all along. A misspelt name FAILS OPEN: it returns the renderer to exactly the founder-versus-void ambiguity the field was added to resolve, silently. Now refused at write time for three cases - a name that is not a layer, a layer on a different grid (a mask must be cell-for-cell with what it masks), and a layer declaring both a background value and an occupancy layer. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12).

column4: The gate refuses a merge while any review thread is unresolved.
column13: Every page is walked; the query no longer stops at the first hundred threads
column14: reviewThreads(first:100) with no pagination made the gate FAIL OPEN past a hundred threads: unseen threads are indistinguishable from resolved ones, so a long-running pull request would have cleared while carrying unread findings. A gate that silently truncates its input is the same defect it exists to catch, and this repository's own rule is that a bounded scan must say what it dropped. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Verified against PR #12 itself: 9 open threads seen, exit 1.

column4: --publish refuses when the run stopped early.
column13: Guard is correct and unchanged; it now has the coverage it never had
column14: The only protection against a timed-out run overwriting the canonical evidence tables in data/calibration/ had NO TEST. It sat inside _report, which imports openmc on its first line and so cannot execute anywhere in the suite - the guard existed and had never once been exercised. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Extracted to a module-level refuse_partial_publish and tested over all four publish/stopped_early combinations, not only the refusing one, since a guard that raised unconditionally would also stop the bad case while making the pilot unpublishable.

column4: The seven fixed colours mean the same organism never changes colour.
column13: One palette slot per id across the spanned range, not one per species present
column14: THE FIXED-PALETTE INVARIANT WAS BROKEN BY THE FIXED-PALETTE CODE. species_legend correctly returns only the species present with their fixed colours, but passing those straight to the renderer with clim spanning the id range distributes them ACROSS it: for ids {1,2,7} three colours spread over six units, so species 2 drew in whatever fell at that fraction while the legend labelled it with the second palette entry - the picture disagreeing with its own key. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). The palette now covers the contiguous id range with half-unit padding, so each id sits in the middle of its own band. Tested as the invariant itself: the same organism must land in the same slot under different subsets.

column4: The bare tier can fail on the render path that pyvista otherwise hides.
column13: Checks LOAD_GLOBAL instructions instead of co_names heuristics
column14: THE CHECK WRITTEN TO CATCH UNRESOLVED NAMES COULD ONLY CATCH ONE. It filtered co_names - which mixes global lookups with attribute names - by requiring a name be UPPERCASE and an actual export of viewer.py. That matched the CATEGORICAL bug in front of it and nothing else: a misspelling like CATGORICAL is not a viewer export and occupied_maks is not uppercase, so both would pass while plot_layer raised NameError on any host with a renderer - the exact skipped surface the test claims to cover. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Now reads LOAD_GLOBAL from the bytecode, which draws the distinction natively, over every function in the module rather than a hand-listed six, with a known-bad function proving it catches both misspelling shapes.

column4: The gate's negative controls exercise the gate.
column13: A fake gh emitting two pages covers the branch PREFLIGHT_FIXTURE bypasses
column14: The fixture hook that made the gate testable also hid the newest thing added to it: every control supplied an already-flattened response, so removing --paginate, $endCursor, pageInfo or the jq fold left all eight green. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12), which is the second finding in a row against the merge gate itself. A fake gh on PATH now emits two pages with the only unresolved thread on page two; removing --paginate reproduces 'Clear to merge' over an open P1.

column4: scan() refuses an unsupported refinement before spending the histories.
column13: Correct and unchanged; a runner spy now proves the ordering
column14: The existing test called _biofilm_scan_mass DIRECTLY, so it passed whether the preflight loop existed or not - delete the loop and scan() reverts to running full transport before refusing, and nothing turns red. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). scan() is now driven with a spy runner that raises if reached; removing the preflight loop makes it fail.

column4: A one-draw scenario is not reported as distinguishable from zero.
column13: Correct and unchanged; extracted to module level and given controls
column14: With m outer draws the test has m-1 degrees of freedom, so one draw has none. Falling back to the normal critical value 3.09 understates the truth at every finite df - at df=1 it is 318.3, a factor of 103 - so a scenario with no degrees of freedom would be declared significant on a test that cannot be performed. The refusal was nested inside _report, whose first statement imports openmc, so it could have been deleted with no suite noticing. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Note the control had to target the RIGHT regression: breaking the df<1 early return alone is invisible, because the table fallback also returns None; only substituting 3.09 exposes it.

column4: Every ratio must divide the finest, checked before any transport.
column13: Correct and unchanged; extracted to module level and given both-direction controls
column14: The only protection against a non-divisor ratio pairing a 4x mass array with a 3x tally - a mismatch that surfaces only after the raytrace and histories are paid for. It sat in main() below import openmc, unreachable from every suite here. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Tested in both directions, since a guard refusing everything would also stop 1,2,4, the ladder the study runs.

column4: species_palette returns a colormap and limits for a species layer.
column13: An all-background layer returns the full palette instead of raising
column14: A species layer of pure background has no ids present, so species_legend returns [] - which the existing out-of-range test already permits - and min() over nothing raised ValueError before the layer could draw. A viewer that crashes on an empty snapshot cannot show that the snapshot is empty, which is a thing a reader needs to see. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12) on the palette fix from the previous round.

column4: A criterion is unmet exactly when the gate has something to say about it.
column13: Criterion 7 matches the three date fields by name, not a bare 'is unset'
column14: MISDIRECTION, NOT SILENCE. approval.problems emits '<field> is unset' for the three dates AND for approval_source_id and approval_scope_hash, and criterion 7 matched the bare phrase - so an approval with no registered document reported criterion 7, ABOUT DATES, as its blocker while criterion 8, about provenance, stayed green. Whoever read that milestone would have gone to fix a date that was never the problem. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Criterion 7 now names the three date fields and approval_source_id maps to criterion 8. The first version of the control did not catch this: asserting the RIGHT criterion is present does not detect an EXTRA one, and it passed against the restored bug. It now also asserts the criteria that are not implicated stay met.

column4: species_palette is empty-safe, so an all-background layer renders.
column13: plot_layer skips add_mesh on a zero-cell dataset and says so on the canvas
column14: THE EMPTY-PALETTE FIX ONLY MOVED THE CRASH ONE LINE DOWN. Thresholding an all-background layer leaves a dataset with zero cells and add_mesh rejects it, so the ValueError became a PyVista error instead. The bare-tier control exercised species_palette([]) rather than plot_layer, verifying the fix one level below where it failed. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12).

column4: The bare tier exercises the whole observer contract; only rendering is gated.
column13: pyvista is a dev dependency and CI runs the render tier under xvfb
column14: EIGHT SILENT SKIPS HID THREE REAL DEFECTS IN ONE SESSION: a NameError on the first line of the render branch, a species palette that mis-slotted every id under an uneven subset, and a crash on an empty field. Each was found by external review rather than by the suite, because pyvista was installed nowhere that ran it and 'N skipped' reads as a neutral fact. pyvista is now in the dev extra and CI runs the tier under xvfb with -rs so the skip list stays visible. Local result: 241 passed, 6 skipped, and all six remaining skips are openmc, not the renderer.

column4: A criterion is unmet exactly when the gate has something to say about it.
column13: Each problem is classified by the field it is ABOUT, not by substrings of the concatenation
column14: AN IDENTIFIER COULD MANUFACTURE A DATE BLOCKER. Matching patterns against ' '.join(problems) meant any echoed field value could trip an unrelated criterion: approval_source_id='expired' produced a provenance-only refusal whose text contained the word, and criterion 7 - about dates - fired on it. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12), one step beyond the REFD-06 fix. Every message is now classified individually by the field named at its head, with only genuine cross-field sentences matched by phrase, and approval_scope_hash splits by message: unset means nothing binds the row (criterion 2) while a mismatch means the approval no longer covers it (criterion 6).

column4: --publish refuses when the run stopped early.
column13: The refusal is now the only route to the canonical directory, not a separate statement
column14: Testing refuse_partial_publish alone proved the predicate and not the wiring: deleting its call left every test green while _report reopened data/calibration/ in write mode after a budget-exhausted run. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). The guard and the target now live in one function, so the canonical directory cannot be obtained without passing the refusal.

column4: A one-draw scenario is not reported as distinguishable from zero.
column13: The verdict itself is tested, not only the critical-value table
column14: t_critical_999(0) is None proves the table; it does not prove the None reaches the verdict. Swapping the call site back to the 3.09 fallback left every table-level test green while a one-draw scenario became reportable as significant. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). The verdict is now one function taking (e2, se, m); the case that matters is m=2 with se=1.0, which must FAIL because at one degree of freedom the critical value is 318.3 rather than 3.09.

column4: Every ratio must divide the finest, checked before any transport.
column13: The check now runs before import openmc, so the refusal is genuinely early
column14: THE GUARD WAS NOT EARLY AND THE HELPER TEST COULD NOT TELL. refuse_non_divisor_ratios sat BELOW import openmc and below load_snapshot, so a bad ratio was discovered only once the heavy stack was up - and never in this tier, because the import fails first. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Ratio parsing needs nothing but the argument string, so it moved above the import; main() is now driven directly with 1,3,4 and the control fails both when the call is deleted AND when it is moved back below the import.

column4: The pagination control exercises real pagination.
column13: The fake refuses a query missing $endCursor or pageInfo before emitting page two
column14: The fake emitted page two on seeing --paginate alone, so deleting $endCursor or the pageInfo selection left the control green while real pagination silently stopped - the same fail-open shape the pagination fix existed to close, reproduced inside its own test. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12), the third finding against the merge gate. Removing either element now fails the control.

column4: Each problem is classified by the field it is about.
column13: Relation phrases are matched only AFTER the field is identified
column14: THE SAME HOLE ONE SIZE SMALLER. The scope-mismatch phrase was tested BEFORE reading the message head, so approval_source_id = 'does not match the conditions' produced a provenance-only refusal that the checklist reported as criterion 6, leaving criterion 8 met. An echoed identifier could still redirect the institutional checklist. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12) on the fix for REFD-07. A phrase may now narrow a message already known to be about a field; it may never decide which field a message is about.

column4: The pagination fake enforces the GraphQL cursor contract.
column13: The fake requires after:$endCursor on the connection, not just the declaration
column14: Checking that $endCursor appeared ANYWHERE was satisfied by the variable declaration alone: remove the after: binding from the connection and cursor updates cannot advance reviewThreads, so the real gate sticks on page one while the control stays green. Codex verified this by removing only the binding and observing all nine controls pass. Fourth finding against the merge gate.

column4: Each problem is classified by the field it is about.
column13: The prefix strip handles both repr quote styles, so the id cannot steer the checklist
column14: THE IDENTIFIER WAS DATA THAT COULD STEER THE VERDICT. approval.problems formats the growth condition id with !r, and Python switches to double quotes when the value contains an apostrophe - so an ordinary id like "O'Brien-1" produced a prefix the classifier's regex could not strip. The head became the word 'condition', nothing classified, and an unset source id was reported as a scope failure plus an UNMAPPED refusal. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12), the third successive narrowing of the same defect: values reaching a decision they should have no part in.

column4: Each problem is classified by the field it is about.
column13: approval.classified carries the subject; nothing parses the prose
column14: FOUR FIXES NARROWED ONE DEFECT WITHOUT CLOSING IT. The checklist recovered each refusal's field by stripping a 'growth condition <id>' prefix and taking the first token. It failed on an echoed field value matching a criterion pattern; then on a longer echoed value impersonating a relation phrase; then on an apostrophe flipping repr to double quotes; then on an id containing BOTH quote characters, which repr must escape and no delimiter pair can bracket. Each fix was correct and each left the shape intact one size smaller, because the defect was never the regex - it was asking a sentence built from unrestricted CSV data to say which field it was about. Caught across four rounds of external review (Codex, PR #12), which recommended the structural fix. approval.classified now returns Refusal(subject, text) and problems() is derived from it, so the two cannot disagree and a condition id is data again. Verified: fourteen single-field breakages give identical correct verdicts under gid 'GC1' and under gid O'Brien "lab".

column4: The refusal is the only route to the canonical directory.
column13: The guard is on the DESTINATION, not on the --publish flag
column14: IT WAS NOT THE ONLY ROUTE. --publish is one way into data/calibration/; --outdir data/calibration is another, and it reached the canonical tables without passing any check at all - so a budget-exhausted run could still overwrite published evidence with partial rows, which is exactly the loss the refusal exists to prevent. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12) on the fix from PILOT-09. A flag is a proxy for the thing that matters; the directory IS the thing that matters. The check now resolves the target and refuses it, along with any subdirectory of it, by whichever route.

column4: A partial scenario set must not replace a complete one.
column13: The completeness check keys on the destination, like the stopped-early check
column14: THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE IN ONE FUNCTION. PILOT-11 moved the stopped-early guard onto the destination and left the OTHER publication prerequisite on args.publish - so a COMPLETED run with --outdir data/calibration and no --publish passed both: the stopped-early check because nothing stopped early, the completeness check because the flag was false. It would then overwrite the canonical CSVs with the default partial scenario set, dropping the rows that published claims cite. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Both prerequisites now route through writes_canonical_tables(args).

column4: background=None means every cell carries information.
column13: UNDECLARED is the default and is refused; None must be stated deliberately
column14: OMISSION ACQUIRED A SEMANTICS. Making None both the default AND the statement 'hide nothing' meant a producer who simply forgot made that claim silently - and two did: omega_b drew its false cells as part of the metric's region, and the upsampled cell_id_on_r* overlay grew a shell of empty space. Neither was hand-written for a test, which is why every fixture-based test passed. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12), which also asked for coverage of the PRODUCED manifest rather than a resembling fixture. UNDECLARED is now the default and bundle_problems refuses it; an AST check reads the producer itself so a new layer cannot omit the declaration.

column4: occupancy_from names the layer that says where biomass is.
column13: The occupancy source must declare background 0, the one encoding the mask implements
column14: A MASK IS NOT A UNIVERSAL READER OF ABSENCE. occupied_mask tests > 0, which encodes one convention: 0 empty, negatives out-of-domain sentinels (cell_id 0 background, -1 wall). occupancy_from was validated for existence and for grid but never for ENCODING, so a source declaring background = -1 - meaning label 0 is valid data - would have had every zero-valued cell silently deleted by the one piece of code that depends on that declaration. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12) on the fix for VIEW-05. Refusing an unsupported encoding is honest; rendering the wrong cells quietly is not.

column4: The occupancy source must declare background 0, the encoding the mask implements.
column13: Both halves are validated: background 0 AND no negative other than -1
column14: I VALIDATED HALF OF A TWO-PART CONTRACT AND TESTED IT WITH DATA THAT COULD NOT EXERCISE THE OTHER HALF. background = 0 says which value is empty; it does not say every negative is a sentinel, and Layer.background cannot, since it names ONE value. The mask tests > 0, so a source using -7 as legitimate data loses those cells silently. The parametrized control used an all-zero array, so the negative half was never touched - the same shape as testing a helper and calling the guard covered. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12) on the fix for VIEW-10. OUT_OF_DOMAIN moved to viewer.py beside the Layer that validates against it, and observer.WALL is now an alias so the two cannot drift.

column4: Interface-area error sits at 0.41-0.51 across a 16x range.
column13: 0.467-0.510 across an 8x range, over the pitches that tile
column14: BOTH HALVES OF THE PUBLISHED RANGE CAME FROM THE WITHDRAWN ROW. 0.41 is the 3.2 um error and 16x is 3.2 -> 0.2. LADDER-04 withdrew that row and I audited only its own headline, twice, leaving a dependent figure contradicting the correction printed beside it. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). Over the pitches that tile the error is 0.467-0.510 across 8x - a NARROWER spread over a SHORTER range, so the conclusion is unchanged and slightly stronger: the error moves less than was reported while still refusing to fall. Withdrawing a row means auditing everything computed from it.

column4: EPS and melanin applied to fruit and seeded vegetables protect against UV as a natural sunscreen and help maintain optimal water activity in drought or heavy rain.
column13: melanin yield per Gy; film thickness; a UV transmittance spectrum; an a_w sorption isotherm; a produce assay
column14: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY BEARS ON IT. The CPM has no yield, no film, no optical property and no water-activity term; 'water activity' and 'sunscreen' appear in zero files. The melanin PRODUCTION rates are separately ledgered at PP-T2-18/19/20 and are all needs_calibration, so even the input this would rest on is uncalibrated. Recorded because an application stated in correspondence is exactly the kind of claim that reaches a paper or a grant without ever being challenged.

column4: D. radiodurans EPS binds or chelates Th-232, as shown in the AM7 paper.
column13: resolve the cited source and record it in data/calibration/spatial/sources.csv with a url or sha256
column14: THE CITATION IS NOT RESOLVABLE FROM WHAT WE HAVE. 'AM7' names no entry in the source registry, and 'chelat' appears in zero files. Thorium IS discussed in the repository, which makes this the more dangerous kind of gap: a real neighbouring topic that an unresolved attribution can attach itself to. Attribution to a paper nobody has retrieved is not evidence - the same rule the approval gate applies to institutional documents.

column4: Bioactives including betaine and proline could be harvested from the consortium.
column13: titres, an extraction route, and a reason the CPM's biomass parcels bear on either compound
column14: Both are osmolytes and neither is a modelled quantity; 'betaine' and 'proline' appear in zero files. The model carries species labels and biomass parcels, not metabolites, so there is no quantity here that could become a titre without a different model.

column4: Growth factors such as NGF and BDNF might eventually be produced and isolated.
column13: a heterologous expression programme, a host, a construct, and an isolation route - none of which is a biofilm morphology question
column14: NGF and BDNF are mammalian neurotrophins. Producing them in a bacterial and fungal consortium is a protein-expression project that shares no premise with this model, not an extension of it. 'BDNF' appears in zero files. Recorded rather than dismissed because the distance between a model and a product claim is exactly what a ledger is for.

column4: Melanin activity can be measured, and the biofilm can be shown to do what we want it to.
column13: a declared assay, and a dynamic observable the model actually represents
column14: The second half is the load-bearing one and it names no observable. 'Does what we want' is not a measurable proposition, and the repository already refuses this shape elsewhere: gate 9 of the online coupling design blocks seconds-per-MCS on a DECLARED dynamic observable for the same reason. PP-T2-18/19/20 gate the melanin RATES; this row gates reading them as a product claim.

column4: A radiotrophic biofilm is economically feasible as a production platform.
column13: any measured yield at all, plus energy, containment and labour costs against a declared product
column14: There is no measured effect to build an economic case on. delta is unset, Reference D is NOT_EVALUATED, CAMPAIGN_READY is no, and the pilot's own verdict is that the effect moves with tally resolution and with region definition. An economic argument resting on that would be certifying the noise that produced it.

column4: A Julia package Radiodialysis.jl would provide a usable radiodialysis model.
column13: fix the units error first: X_total is a site fraction and must become a concentration; then declare the membrane m-vs-P_eff constitutive choice
column14: THE REPOSITORY'S OWN GATE ALREADY ANSWERS THIS. materials/report.evaluate() returns RADIODIALYSIS: BLOCKED unconditionally, and says why: 'blocked by a units error, not by missing data'. A measured rho_wet and w_water CANNOT be plumbed into a field that is still a site fraction, so no amount of measurement clears it - the model change comes first. A STOP CONDITION additionally forbids OpenMC dose entering the radiodialysis model until m vs P_eff is declared. Packaging it now would package a model this repository says is not ready, with the package name asserting the opposite. SEPARATELY, the same correspondence asked whether a gamma GRADIENT can be introduced in a bioreactor at all. That is an open question and is recorded here as one; it must not become a claim by sitting next to claims.

column4: Out-of-range species ids are dropped, not coloured.
column13: plot_layer masks to the legend's range, so what is drawn is what the legend describes
column14: THE LEGEND DROPPED THE LABEL AND THE PICTURE KEPT IT. species_legend filters an id outside 1..7 and a bare-tier test asserted exactly that - but plot_layer passed the whole occupied dataset to add_mesh, so a cell labelled 9 still rendered, in whatever colour its value landed on, with nothing in the key to explain it. The legend test and the picture disagreed and only the legend was ever checked. A viewer showing an organism it cannot name is worse than one showing fewer cells, because the reader counts it. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). The legend's own span is the valid range by construction, so thresholding to it drops exactly what the legend dropped and nothing else; the control now drives plot_layer and counts rendered cells.

column4: What is drawn is what the legend describes.
column13: The legend is built from the cells that survive masking, not from the raw field
column14: TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS OF ONE FACT. species_legend read the raw array while the mesh was built from the occupied cells, and they agreed only while no producer declared a background inside the species range. With values {1,9} and background 1 the raw field still offered species 1 to the legend though occupied had dropped it, so the resulting bounds selected NOTHING and add_mesh was handed the empty dataset it rejects. With {1,2} and background 1 the same gap instead listed species 1 in a picture that does not contain it. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12), immediately after the VIEW-12 fix that closed the out-of-range half of the same split. The legend now reads occupied's own cell data: one source, so they cannot disagree.

column4: The coarsest pitch inside tolerance, and inside it at every finer pitch.
column13: A refused pitch is excluded from the convergence tail instead of counting as a failure
column14: ABSENCE OF AN OBSERVATION WAS READ AS AN OBSERVATION OF FAILURE. A refused rung carries no within_* key, and row.get(key, False) made it indistinguishable from a measurement that missed tolerance - breaking the tail beneath it. Inserting a non-tiling 1.4 between 1.6 and 0.8 dragged component size from 1.6 to 0.8 with neither valid measurement changed. The default ladder hid it because its only skipped pitch, 3.2, sits at the coarse END with no tail below it. Caught by external review (Codex, PR #12). SEPARATELY, this function computed a running result in a first loop and DISCARDED it, returning a value from a second unfiltered loop - so the first fix changed nothing and the test failed with the correction apparently in place. The dead loop is gone. Published figures are unchanged: 0.8, 0.4, never, 1.6.

column4: A Colletotrichum challenge assay is the decisive test for the produce-coating claim in RDX-APP-01.
column13: read the registered sources in full, then establish which Colletotrichum species dominate postharvest anthracnose on the named crops - that part was NOT searched
column14: SHARPER THAN THE UV TEST THE CORRESPONDENCE PROPOSED, and capable of falsifying the claim outright. Colletotrichum is an anthracnose genus on high-water-activity fruit, the produce class RDX-APP-01 names. Sources LUDWIG_2014_CGRAM_MELANIN, CGLOEO_2023_DHN_TURGOR, CGSCD1_2020_PATHOGENICITY and CHIGG_2023_PKS_THR1 are registered but were reached at ABSTRACT LEVEL ONLY; the crop-dominance question was not searched at all, because web access was cut off mid-task. needs_verification, not supported - the row records a research direction, not a result.

column4: Melanin applied to produce is protective, acting as a natural sunscreen.
column13: evidence that EXOGENOUS melanin protects produce - not searched, and not implied by anything below
column14: THE NEAREST LITERATURE RUNS THE OTHER WAY. In Colletotrichum, DHN-melanin pathway knockouts ATTENUATE PATHOGENICITY across two species (CGSCD1_2020_PATHOGENICITY; CHIGG_2023_PKS_THR1), so melanin in this system is a fungal virulence requirement rather than a plant protectant. That does NOT show applied melanin helps a pathogen - appressorial melanin is synthesised in situ in a specific wall layer and exogenous material is unlikely to substitute - but it removes the intuition the claim rests on. Same pathway already ledgered at PP-T2-20 (A. niger, DHN-melanin). CORRECTION TO MY OWN SUMMARY: I first described melanin as letting the appressorium build turgor to punch through the cuticle. That is the Magnaporthe account; LUDWIG_2014_CGRAM_MELANIN specifically contradicts it for C. graminicola (albino mutants generated turgor but could not penetrate intact leaves), while CGLOEO_2023_DHN_TURGOR reports expansion pressure falling from 13.02 to 7.34-9.34 MPa in knockouts. The two disagree on mechanism; only the pathogenicity claim survives both, and only that is relied on here.

column4: Adding a phytopathogen to the seven-species consortium is covered by the existing approval scope.

column14: THE DRAFT OF THIS CLAIM WAS AN ABSENCE AND THE ABSENCE WAS FALSE. It read "no aqueous-corrosion study of irradiated FeCrAl found", and its own search returned one on the first page: Corrosion Science 174 (2020) 108824, "Early corrosion behaviour of irradiated FeCrAl alloy in a simulated pressurized water reactor environment", which finds a Cr-rich oxide absent from the as-received alloy, a duplex hematite / Cr-rich-spinel structure, and SEVERE later-stage corrosion from irradiation-induced defects. Two more sit beside it (J Nucl Mater S0022311519316356 on radiation damage plus water radiolysis in hydrogenated water; npj Mater Degrad 2024 on additively manufactured FeCrAl out-of-pile). The draft would have carried a false absence to a reader who works on these alloys. IT WAS ONLY CAUGHT BECAUSE THIS CLAIM WAS GIVEN ITS OWN SEARCH: it shares no terms with HOFFMAN-12, which is microbial, and borrowing HOFFMAN-12 scope would have been false as well as wrong. The replacement is a positive finding and needs no scope. The residual absence - the same question at 30-50 C pool water, or with a biofilm - was not returned by the query "irradiated FeCrAl aqueous corrosion spent fuel pool water" on 2026-08-30. Supporting surface change: HOFFMAN-14 in the ledger sense, alpha-prime, verified at Field/Briggs/Edmondson, Scripta Mater S1359646217304761, Alkrothal 720 and Kanthal APMT to 7.0 dpa at 320-382 C by SANS, model-alloy cluster Cr 51.1-62.5 at percent. CORRECTED SAME DAY, AND THE SENTENCE WAS WRITTEN FROM A SUMMARY RATHER THAN THE METHOD. The memo said 'irradiation makes aqueous corrosion of FeCrAl worse'. Reading Corros. Sci. 174:108824's method shows THREE things the sentence dropped. (1) MODE: 400-keV Fe+ IONS at 400 C, not neutrons - at that energy the damage is a near-surface layer a few hundred nanometres deep, not a bulk-irradiated coupon, so transfer to a real assembly is far weaker than the sentence implied. (2) STAGE DEPENDENCE: the irradiated alloy corroded MORE SLOWLY at first, a Cr-rich oxide plus an ion-sputtered smooth surface suppressing it, with severe corrosion only later - and part of that early behaviour is a sample-preparation artifact rather than a property of irradiated material in service. (3) The footnote attached Field/Briggs/Edmondson's NEUTRON alpha-prime work to the same claim, putting two irradiation modes in one citation. THE FIX IS NOT TO DROP THE CITATION: removing it and leaving alpha-prime plus 'what makes the pool question a real question' would let a reader infer nobody has looked, when someone has, badly, in the wrong conditions. Weak evidence and no evidence are different states and that distinction is this memo's whole discipline. The sentence now says the work exists, at reactor conditions and without a film, and the residual gap names all THREE conditions - pool temperature, a biofilm, and either surface - because naming only the temperature would let the gap read as a thermal complaint. ALPHA-PRIME IS MICROSTRUCTURE AND NOTHING MORE: that source reports no passive-film composition, so 'changes the surface a film would sit on' is an inference it does not make and is not written. FOURTH INSTANCE ON THIS BRANCH OF ONE FAMILY - a claim written from a summary instead of the source - after HOFFMAN-01 (invented '34 months' and a plant name), HOFFMAN-02 (wrong paper, wrong first author), and a commit message describing a fix the commit did not contain. That family produces CONFIDENT FALSE SPECIFICS, which a careful reader cannot discount the way they can discount an overreach, and it is a different failure from the one tools/absence_gate.py catches. ALSO CAUGHT BY THAT GAP: the replacement phrasing considered first, 'what makes the pool question a real question', carries no absence marker at all, so the gate would not have surfaced it while it functioned as an absence claim - the incompleteness now recorded in KNOWN_UNHANDLED, biting on the same diff that records it.
